distribution: Yaxian and Tongshi, Mount Jianfeng, and Mount Mihou in Dongfang, Hainan.
soldier: Sclerotisation of the whole body very weak. Head pale yellow, the two condylar spots nearly blackish brown, the frontal gland area dirty white and spread out like a folding fan; thorax and abdomen almost semi-transparent, the coiled gut visible through the cuticle. Body surface covered with hairs throughout, those on the postclypeus and pronotum stouter, those on the vertex, antennae and legs denser. Head nearly circular; in profile both the postclypeus and the anteclypeus are raised, with a clear concave margin between them. Antennae 14 segments. On the left mandible the angle between the posterior margin of the apical tooth and the anterior cutting edge of marginal tooth 1 is less than a right angle, marginal tooth 2 minute; on the right mandible the corresponding structures meet at an acute angle, the anterior cutting edge of marginal tooth 1 inclined inwards with the tooth point directed upwards. Left mandible changing from flattened to round, becoming flattened and slightly widened again in the anterior middle section, the end concave and forming a small inward hook; right mandible slightly shorter, the body gradually rounded towards the apex, the tip curved downwards and pointed. Postmentum rather long, the hammer-shaped part large, its widest part about twice the narrowest. Pronotum typically saddle-shaped, the middle of the anterior margin slightly concave, the posterior margin nearly straight. Abdomen slender and long, its widest part wider than the thorax and narrower than the head.
taxonomy_note: The scientific name is set as Sinocapritermesparvulus in the original work, an artefact of line-breaking; it refers to the same species as the name used on this site, and the genus name is unchanged.
